title: Toss Strange Coins
statement:
You hold a set of biased coins: coin `i` comes up heads with probability `prob[i]`, independently of the others. Every coin is tossed exactly once. Return the probability that the number of coins showing heads is exactly `target`.

An answer within `10^-5` of the true probability is accepted.
constraints: Answers within 10^-5 of the correct value are accepted
notes:
## Intuition

Listing all `2^n` head/tail outcomes and adding up their probabilities is correct but hopeless for 1000 coins. Instead, ask how the distribution of head counts changes when one more coin is tossed: a count of `heads` after the new coin came either from `heads` before it plus a tail, or from `heads - 1` before it plus a head. That is a 0/1 knapsack where each coin is an item that adds 0 or 1 to the count, weighted by its probability.

## Approach

1. Let `dp[heads]` be the probability of exactly `heads` heads among the coins seen so far, for `heads` from `0` to `target` (larger counts can never come back down, so they are not needed). Start with `dp[0] = 1`.
2. For each coin `p`, update `heads` from `target` down to `1`: `dp[heads] = dp[heads] * (1 - p) + dp[heads - 1] * p`. Going downward means `dp[heads - 1]` still holds the value from before this coin.
3. Update `dp[0]` last: zero heads stays zero only on a tail.
4. Return `dp[target]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`prob = [0.4]`, `target = 1`, so `dp = [1, 0]`. For the coin `p = 0.4`: `dp[1] = 0 * 0.6 + 1 * 0.4 = 0.4`, then `dp[0] = 1 * 0.6 = 0.6`. The answer is `dp[1] = 0.4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · target): each coin updates at most `target + 1` entries.
- Space: O(target) for the single row.

## Pitfalls

- Looping `heads` upward reuses a value already updated for this coin, as if the coin could land heads twice.
- `dp[0]` has no `heads - 1` term; handle it separately instead of reading `dp[-1]`.
- Coins with `p = 0` or `p = 1` are legal; the formula handles them without special cases.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dp[heads]` | probability of exactly `heads` heads among the coins processed so far |
| `p` | heads probability of the current coin |
| `heads` | the head count being updated |

narration.2: dp[heads] will hold the probability of exactly heads heads; only counts up to target matter.
narration.3: Before any coin is tossed, zero heads is certain.
narration.5: Add the coins one at a time, like items in a 0/1 knapsack.
narration.6: Go from target down to 1 so dp[heads - 1] still describes the coins before this one.
narration.7: Either the count was already heads and this coin shows tails, or it was heads - 1 and this coin shows heads.
narration.9: Zero heads survives only if this coin shows tails.
narration.12: After every coin, dp[target] is the probability of exactly target heads.
